sentences.text:
The present Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a writ or order or direction more particularly in the nature of writ of mandamus declaring the action of the respondent failure to take action pursuant to the communication sent by the 5th respondent vide R2/691/2017, dated 08.09.2017 with reference to the revised estimate made by the Executive Engineer, R & B Division, Siricilla, Rajanna Siricilla District as illegal and arbitrary and consequently direct the respondents to consider the proceedings in R2/691/2017 dated 08.09.2017 to pay the compensation by taking into consideration of the revised estimates which were made in respect of D.No.7-64/1 of Cheerlavancha Village, Thangallapally Mandal, Siricilla District ..."

2. Heard Sri B.Arjun Rao, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Panchayat Raj and Rural Development appearing for the respondents, and perused the record.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the owners and possessors of Vamshikrishna Video Theatre, which was constructed in the year, 1995 by obtaining valid permission from the Gram Panchayat.
On completion of construction, D.No.7-64/1 was assigned from the Competent Authority to run the above said video theatre.

While it being so, the respondent-authorities have been issued Gazette Notification bearing No.52 dated 13.06.2006 notifying the villages, which were affected fully or partially under Mid Manair Reservoir Project,
wherein the Village of the petitioners was also notified as fully affected Village under the said Project.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that in view of the acquisition of the structures of the aforesaid project, it affected the video theatre of the petitioners which was wrongly estimated due to typographical error of the year of construction, which was mentioned as 1971 instead of 1995 and for which the age of the structure was mentioned as 36 years and 35% of the estimated value of the property was deducted towards depreciation, which quantifying the compensation.
But, the fact remains that the permission itself is granted in the year, 1994, as per Panchayat records and the same was constructed in the year, 1995.
In view of the same, the petitioners have submitted an application for correcting the typographical error to the respondent-authorities.

During the pendency of the said application, the respondent No.3 having Kadapathri Sudhakar Rao vs The State Of Telangana, on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53283049/
1 found that there was a clerical error and taken the possession of the property of the petitioners and issued notice to the petitioners to receive the compensation subject to the rectification of the clerical error.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, under protest subject to the correcting the clerical error and received the cheque on 31.12.2017.
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that the petitioners had made a representation dated 08.09.2017 to the respondent No.2/District Collector.

In view of the above representation, the respondent No.2 addressed a letter to the respondent No.5/District Panchayat Officer to verify the age of the building with reference to the Panchayat records.

Subsequently, the respondent No.5 addressed a letter dated 08.09.2017 to the respondent No.2 stating that Vamshikrishna Video Theatre bearing Door No.7-64/1 has been examined and found that the construction of the said theatre was made in the year, 1995 and requested to take appropriate decision for correction of the age of the building.
Even after sending the communication on 08.09.2017, the respondent No.2 failed to take any action.
Thereafter, the petitioners made representations from time to time for fixing the age of the structure as 12 years as on 2007.
The action of the respondents in not taking decision as per Panchayat records is illegal and arbitrary and requested to allow the writ petition.

6. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondent Nos.1 to 4, basing on the counter-affidavit, submits that after passing of the award, a report from the respondent No.5/District Panchayat Officer to the respondent No.2/District Collector has been received on 15.09.2017, stating that the construction of the said structure bearing No.7-64/1 was made in the year, 1995.

In view of the same, the matter was referred to the Executive Engineer, R&B,
Siricilla for taking necessary action, who in return furnished another estimate by reducing the percentage of depreciation from 35% to 11.25% which will cause an enhancement of about Rs.20.8 lakhs.

In view of the same, the petitioners have to avail the remedy under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (for brevity, 'the Act, 2013').
7.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition further submits that on receipt of the notice under Section 37(e) of the Act, 2013 vide reference No.A1/1817/2017-VII Abadi, dated 11.08.2017, the petitioners did not turned out to receive the award compensation up to 28.12.2017 and 29.12.2017, they had filed a petition along with a notarized affidavit to the respondents for payment of award compensation.
Accordingly, the award compensation has been paid.

The petitioners received the same without any protest and filed petitions on 30.12.2017 and 08.01.2018 and requested the respondent-authorities to refer the matter under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

9.
